Councillors have voted to refuse a controversial 199-home development plan for Ramsey despite receiving a recommendation for approval. BDW Trading Ltd submitted the proposal for land south of The Malting with landowners Susan and Robert Pickard. The scheme included up to 199 homes, 40 per cent affordable housing, children’s play areas, drainage infrastructure and related works. Developers also proposed a landscaped perimeter, a 1.1km circular walking route linked to public rights of way and green infrastructure covering around 37 per cent of the site. The site is land south of The Malting in Ramsey However, at a meeting on October 19, Huntingdonshire District Council's Development Management Committee voted to refuse the outline application, which had been recommended for approval. Planning officers said the benefits outweighed the harm, pointing to Huntingdonshire’s current shortfall in five-year housing land supply. The report said the scheme would help meet housing need and provide substantial affordable housing. Cllr Andrew Wood proposed refusing the plan against officers’ recommendation, subject to consultation with the Secretary of State.
